fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the road entrance to the driveway so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to make the turnoff visible at night or in low-visibility conditions.
• Post a site map near the driveway entrance showing the locations of both structures, parking areas, and any gate or fence access points.
• Keep the circular driveway clear of parked vehicles so fire apparatus and ambulances can pull through without reversing.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the access drive to maintain overhead clearance for emergency vehicles the full length of the driveway.
• Cut back dense vegetation along both sides of the access drive so responders have a clear path to both structures on foot.
• Identify and mark a turnaround point near the detached structure so apparatus drivers know where to position without blocking their exit.
• Install a gate lock box or use a standardized lock at any fenced entry point so responders can open it without forcing entry.
• Keep a gate or opening in the perimeter fencing at the rear of the property so responders can reach the back of the main residence on foot.
• Mark the location of any exterior utility shutoffs on both structures so responders can find them without searching.
• Keep walkways between the main residence and detached structure clear of stored items,

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly against or within a few feet of any structure in the cluster.
• Thin trees within the tree cluster closest to the structures to create more open space between individual trees.
• Remove brush from the brush area where it connects toward the structures.
• Clear any dead or dry plant material from the base of shrubs and trees near the buildings.
• Keep the long driveway free of overhanging branches so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Cut back scattered shrubs along the driveway edges that could block access or movement.
• Separate shrubs and small trees that grow in a continuous line between the brush area and the structures.
• Thin scattered trees near the structures so their canopies do not touch or overlap each other.
• Keep the open terrain areas around the structures free of new shrub or brush growth.
• Remove any piles of cut vegetation, wood, or debris left near the structures after maintenance work.
